title: India's record 114 Asian Para Games medals: Modi meets athletes in Delhi
dek: India won 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals in Aichi-Nagoya and finished fourth, with five world records. Athletes say the next target is the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympics.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi met India's contingent from the Asian Para Games 2026 in New Delhi on Thursday, after the team brought home 114 medals from Aichi-Nagoya in Japan, the country's best result at the Games. The haul of 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals placed India fourth on the medals table, The Tribune reported.

"This journey from 14 to 114 medals is the result of the pinnacle of your hard work," Modi told the athletes at the Indira Gandhi Sports Complex, according to the Prime Minister's Office. India won 14 medals, including one gold, at the 2010 Asian Para Games; its previous best was 108 at Hangzhou in 2022.

## The record in numbers

According to the Prime Minister's Office release on the meeting, the contingent set five world records and nine Asian records. Thirty-four of the 56 women in the team won medals, as did 36 of the 61 athletes competing at the Games for the first time. Indian athletes took all three podium places in four events and won nine gold medals on the final day alone.

Athletes supported by the Sports Ministry's Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) won 41 medals, and athletes from the Khelo India programme won 19, the release said.

## Standout performances

In para-badminton, Nitesh Kumar won the men's singles SL3 gold, beating compatriot and reigning world champion Pramod Bhagat 21-18, 21-16 in the final. Shooter Mona Agarwal won the women's 50m rifle three positions SH1 gold with world and Asian Para Games records. Haney won the men's javelin F37/38 with a world record, and Sandeep set a world record on debut to win the men's 400m T64.

Modi singled out Rinku, who won gold days after his mother died and held up her photograph on the podium. "That moment made all of us emotional," he said.

## What the athletes said

Nishad Kumar, who won double gold in the men's long jump and high jump T47, said such meetings "motivate us". Shot putter Ayush Verma, who won gold in the F53 class and a javelin bronze, said the meeting "will definitely motivate us for LA". Bhagyashri Jadhav, India's flagbearer at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, where she did not win a medal, took silver in the women's shot put F34 and said the perception of para-athletes had changed: "There used to be pity for us divyangs, but now it feels we are special," she told The Tribune.

## What comes next

The next target is the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympics, where India won a record 29 medals at the previous edition in Paris. Modi said Avani and Manish had already secured quota places for Los Angeles. He also urged that sports equipment and apparel for Indian athletes be made in India, pointing to the Khelo India sports goods manufacturing scheme, which the release says is worth more than Rs 1,800 crore. "The country is with you, and the entire country is waiting for your next victory," he said.
